standard.title: Consent and respectful relationships
standard.description: examine how strategies, such as communicating choices, seeking, giving and denying consent, and expressing opinions and needs can support the development of respectful relationships, including sexual relationships
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can evaluate emotional responses and refine emotion management strategies (AC9HP10P06), and have previously explained and applied assertive consent communication skills (AC9HP8P07). At Y9-10 the focus expands to examining how consent communication strategies support the development of respectful relationships broadly, including sexual relationships.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students examine how communicating choices, seeking, giving and denying consent, and expressing opinions and needs support respectful relationships, including understanding legal requirements and the importance of taking responsibility for their own actions.

nodes.label: Consent communication strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and refine strategies for communicating consent clearly and respectfully across a range of relationship scenarios
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one strategy for communicating consent clearly in a specific relationship scenario; explain what makes it effective
nodes.typical_width: Refine strategies for communicating choices, needs and opinions clearly and respectfully across peer group, family and work situations; describe strategies that enhance safety and wellbeing of sexual partners including communicating feelings, respecting boundaries, gaining affirmative consent, and assertive communication; reflect on taking responsibility for own actions
wider: Investigate the legal requirements for consent in your state or territory — including seeking, giving, refusing and accepting refusal in online and offline interactions with friends, colleagues, strangers and intimate partners — and evaluate how these laws connect to respectful relationship principles
Rehearse consent communication in scenarios where social pressure or power imbalances are present — evaluate which strategies are most effective and why
Examine how consent communication strategies need to adapt for digital contexts (texting, social media, online relationships) where verbal and non-verbal cues are absent
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot articulate and refine specific consent communication strategies cannot examine their relationship-building function in Node 2 — the examination of how strategies support relationships requires first having identified what those strategies actually are.

response_modes.reason: Consent communication is a capability that requires a repertoire across relationship types and contexts. Peer group, family, intimate partner, and online contexts each require different communication approaches. The legal dimension (state/territory requirements) adds a factual layer that students need alongside the skills dimension. Building range across contexts is more valuable than polishing a single scenario response.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Legal requirements investigation, power-imbalanced scenarios, and digital consent contexts each add a genuinely different dimension to consent communication. Students who engage the wider tier understand that consent is not a single skill applied uniformly but a set of context-sensitive practices with legal, social and technological dimensions.
success_criteria: Describes at least one specific consent communication strategy with reference to a named scenario type
Strategy includes both verbal and non-verbal components, or explicitly addresses what to do when non-verbal cues are absent
Reflects on taking responsibility for own behaviour — not only on what others should do

nodes.label: Consent supporting respectful relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine how consent communication strategies support the development of respectful relationships, including sexual relationships
nodes.minimum_width: Explain one way in which practising consent communication supports the development of a more respectful relationship
nodes.typical_width: Examine how strategies for communicating choices, seeking and denying consent, and expressing needs support respectful relationships broadly and sexual relationships specifically; reflect on potential impact of own behaviour on others; examine how consent communication connects to affirmative consent, individual rights, and mutual respect
wider: Examine how the portrayal of consent in TV shows, movies, popular music and online content may influence people's beliefs about what respectful and consensual relationships look like — evaluate the gap between media representations and legal/ethical standards

Investigate how consent and respectful communication functions differently in relationships where power is unequal (e.g. age gaps, social status, online anonymity) and evaluate what additional strategies are needed
Design a peer education resource on consent for a specific audience (e.g. Year 8 students, parents/carers) — evaluate what framing and examples would be most effective

response_modes.reason: This node integrates consent communication skills (Node 1) with the broader relationship development framework — showing how practising consent is not a procedural compliance exercise but is constitutive of respectful relationships. Students who can communicate consent but cannot explain its relational function have not reached the descriptor's command term. The integration task is connecting the skill to the relationship quality it produces.

success_criteria: Explains a specific connection between practising consent communication and a quality of the relationship it builds
Includes sexual relationships as one context — does not treat consent as relevant only to intimate relationships
Reflects on own responsibility — not only on what makes a relationship respectful in the abstract
